purpose: Cefazolin is an antibiotic used to treat or prevent bacterial infections. It is commonly used for skin infections, bone infections, heart valve infections, urinary tract infections, and to prevent infections before and after surgery. It only works against bacterial infections, not viral ones like colds or the flu.
how_it_works: Cefazolin works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria. Think of the bacterial wall like a protective shell — cefazolin punches holes in that shell, causing the bacteria to fall apart and die. Because human cells do not have this type of wall, the antibiotic targets the bacteria without directly harming your own cells.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site, upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, and mild skin rash. Some people may notice a mild fever or headache as well.
warnings: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to penicillin or any other antibiotics, as you may also be allergic to cefazolin. Seek emergency help right away if you develop hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing, as these could be signs of a serious allergic reaction. Also let your healthcare team know if you have kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. If you develop severe or persistent diarrhea, contact your doctor, as this could signal a serious gut infection.
typical_dosing: Cefazolin is given as an injection into a vein (IV) or into a muscle (IM) — it is not taken by mouth. Doses typically range from 250 mg to 2,000 mg (2 grams) every 6 to 12 hours, depending on the type and severity of your infection. Your doctor or nurse will determine the right dose and schedule for you based on your condition and kidney function.
